fields.meta_title: HVAC Landing Page Builder for Repairs and Quotes | Emergent
fields.meta_description: An HVAC landing page turns an ad click into a booked service call or a quote request. See four contractor examples and build yours by prompt.
fields.h1: Build an HVAC Landing Page That Books Repairs and Quotes
fields.hero_description: Get an HVAC landing page that books service calls and quote requests, with each one saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an HVAC Page Needs to Book the Job
fields.features_subheading: Six parts take a homeowner from a broken furnace to a request the dispatcher can schedule, and Emergent changes each by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A first question about what broke

Open the form with fixed choices: No heat, No cooling, Strange noise, or Tune-up. The answer tells the dispatcher how fast to call back, before the visitor has typed a word.
fields.feature_2:
A phone number one tap away

Show the number as a button on the first screen for the homeowner who wants to call instead of typing. Repeat it in the footer, so the number is there wherever the visitor stops.
fields.feature_3:
A row for every request

Each request lands in a database you own with the problem picked, the ZIP code, and the minute it arrived. Your office works the list top to bottom and marks each row Scheduled.
fields.feature_4:
An alert to whoever is on call

Send new requests to the dispatcher by email, to a Slack channel for the office, or to both. The alert carries the homeowner's name and number, plus the problem they picked.
fields.feature_5:
Hours that match the phones

Print the hours someone answers the phone beside the form, plus any after-hours line. A homeowner at 10 pm then knows whether to call now or book a visit for the morning.
fields.feature_6:
A web address homeowners recognize

Publish the page on a domain you already own, such as a booking subdomain of the site customers see on your trucks. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Petra hears about no-heat calls after 6 pm

Tarnhill Heating & Air puts one question first: what is wrong? After 6 pm, a visitor who picks No heat sets off an email to Petra Brenner, the on-call dispatcher, with the homeowner's number in it. Every other problem waits on the morning list. Last night 11 requests came in after 6 pm, and 4 of them picked No heat.
fields.tab_content_2:
Systems 15 years or older go to Joaquin

Corran Bay Comfort asks for the age of the system and the fuel it runs on before it takes an install quote request. Every request for a system 15 years or older goes to Joaquin Teller, the comfort advisor who sets up in-home estimates. This month 23 of 38 quote requests went to Joaquin, and 15 went to the repair desk.
fields.tab_content_3:
No form for the 8 visitors outside the area

Saltbrook Air works inside 9 ZIP codes, so its page asks for the ZIP before it shows the booking form. A ZIP on the list opens the form, and any other ZIP brings up the list of the 9 the company serves. This week 52 visitors entered a ZIP: 44 saw the form and 8 saw the list.
fields.tab_content_4:
30 tune-ups booked by the search ad

Marlow Creek Heating ran its $119 fall furnace tune-up in a search ad and on a postcard mailer, and each points to the page with its own tag. The form saves that tag on the booking row, where the homeowner never sees it. Of 47 bookings so far, 30 came from the search ad and 17 from the postcard.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an HVAC Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to an HVAC landing page that books repair calls and install quotes from homeowners inside your service area.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one job for each page
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Size the call button for a thumb
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give repair calls and install quotes their own pages, and point each ad at the page for its job. A homeowner with a dead furnace wants a call back tonight, not a financing chart for a new system.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Make the first field a short set of choices, such as No heat or No cooling, instead of an open box. The choice decides who hears about the request. Put it ahead of the name and the phone number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Make the button at least the size Lighthouse treats as safe: tap targets that are 48 px by 48 px never fail the audit. Where the number sits in structured data, Google writes: be sure to include the country code and area code in the phone number.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the ZIP before the rest of the form, and tag the field with the postal-code autocomplete token so the browser can fill it. MDN describes that token as a postal code (in the United States, this is the ZIP code).
fields.howto_step_5_des: List the hours someone picks up next to the form, with the after-hours number if you run one. If that line never closes, Google's local business docs explain in the markup section how to show a business as open 24 hours a day.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Keep the repair form to the problem, a name, a phone number, and the ZIP. Ask how old the system is and which fuel it burns only on the install quote page, where the comfort advisor uses them to plan the estimate.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and book a test call
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the jobs, the ZIP codes, and who hears about each request, and Emergent builds the page from that prompt. Send a test request from a phone, then check the row in your database and the email to the dispatcher.

faq_plan.q: What is a hvac landing page?
faq_plan.a: An HVAC landing page is a single web page that asks a homeowner to book one heating or cooling job, such as a repair call or an install quote. It pairs that offer with a short form under a call button, and leaves out the menu that leads to the rest of the company's site.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a hvac landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide which job the page books and which ZIP codes you serve, then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder, along with who should hear about each request. Emergent builds the page and its database from that prompt, and you change any part of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should the form on an HVAC landing page ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what the dispatcher needs to call back and pick a technician, which on a repair page comes to four fields. Leave equipment details and gate codes for the call itself, where the homeowner can explain them. On a page Emergent builds, each answer is saved as a column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should an HVAC landing page offer a referral reward?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you can tell which bookings the reward brought in. Give each customer a link to share, and have the form save it with the booking so you know whom to thank. A referral landing page runs on the same idea: the visitor arrives through a friend's link, and the page records whose link it was.

faq_plan.q: How should an HVAC landing page handle emergency calls at night?
faq_plan.a: Put a phone number first and treat the form as the backup. Show the after-hours line above the form, and have a No heat or No cooling request email whoever is on call that night. The app Emergent builds can send that alert to the dispatcher's inbox or post it in Slack.

faq_plan.q: Should an HVAC landing page show prices?
faq_plan.a: Show a price for fixed-price jobs, such as a tune-up, and leave install work to a quote after a visit. Print the cost of a diagnostic visit too, if you charge one. The homeowner then knows it before the technician knocks.

faq_plan.q: Should an HVAC landing page include a video?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if it is short and sits next to the form instead of in place of it. Film a technician introducing the company in under a minute, and keep the call button in view while it plays. A podcast landing page puts one episode player beside one subscribe button in the same way.

faq_plan.q: What should an HVAC landing page say after someone books?
faq_plan.a: Say when someone will call and what to do if it cannot wait. Name the window, such as within the hour during business hours, and repeat the after-hours number for anyone without heat. Add a line on what to have ready, such as the model printed on the furnace label.

faq_plan.q: What should an HVAC landing page show to earn a homeowner's trust?
faq_plan.a: Show proof a homeowner can check: photos of your own technicians and trucks, and reviews signed with a first name and a town. Add the warranty terms you offer on your own work, in plain words, and skip stock photos of people who do not work for you.

faq_plan.q: Do repairs and installs each need their own HVAC landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once each job has its own ads. A repair page sells a fast visit and an install page sells an estimate, and each needs its own form. Treat each as a service landing page built around one job and one form. Emergent builds the second page from a prompt, and you change either one by prompting again.

plan.angle: Searchers for hvac landing page get website-design roundups, template galleries and one paid-traffic checklist that show how an HVAC page looks, never what happens to a request after the visitor taps the button. This page shows four HVAC landing pages built around booking logistics (a no-heat call that emails the on-call dispatcher, a replacement quote form that routes by system age, a ZIP code check that keeps out-of-area jobs off the schedule, a fall tune-up offer that records which ad booked it), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, then gives the build steps a contractor needs. It makes no code, efficiency, rebate or licensing claims. Plumber, electrician, roofing and contractor pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
